title: Lease-drain protocol for limiter failover and proportional shedding
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add a short-lived lease-based drain protocol and proportional shedding policy to improve availability when primary regional limiters or quota controllers are degraded or unreachable. The protocol allows healthy regions to acquire temporary leases to accept and drain in-flight traffic in a controlled, SLO-aware manner while preserving fairness across tenants and preventing amplification during global incidents.
rationale: Recent incidents showed single-region limiter outages caused either wholesale fail-open (breaking SLOs) or aggressive global shedding with poor fairness. We need a middle path: (1) limit the blast radius, (2) enable predictable capacity handoff, (3) maintain proportional tenant fairness, and (4) respect SLO prioritization for critical customers.
design_decisions: 1) Lease semantics: 2s-8s TTL leases with renewable heartbeats; broken leases are fast-detected. 2) Proportional shedding: per-tenant weights derived from commit metadata and SLO tier; shedding preserves relative allocation across tenants. 3) Circuit hysteresis: two-tier CB with short immediate open (100-500ms) and longer degraded window (5-30s) to avoid flapping. 4) Drain window: bounded per-lease drain budget (max tokens/time) to prevent unlimited burst transfer. 5) Fallback model: when leases exhausted, degrade to token-bucket soft-shedding honoring P0 customers.
implementation_notes:
- New component: regional-lease-manager (stateless control plane service backed by strongly-consistent store for lease coordination).
- Changes in limiter hot path: accept lease token header, consult local lease budget cache, and apply proportional quota decrement.
- Backpressure: integrate with existing admission controller so that request paths can be fast-failed during degraded mode rather than blocking threads.
- Lightweight serialization: lease metadata packed into 64-bit tag to avoid GC pressure.
- Feature flag: runtime.feature.regional_lease_v1 rollout, default off for hostedsandbox.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for lease expiration/renewal and proportional allocator.
- Integration test: two-region testbed where primary limiter is killed and secondary acquires lease and drains a configurable backlog; validate no more than 10% extra token consumption vs steady state.
- Chaos test: introduce network partition and flappy leader; ensure hysteresis avoids oscillation.
- Load test: can sustain expected peak-10% with lease draining enabled.
- SLO validation: synthetic tenants across tiers (P0/P1/P2) show prioritized success rates during failover windows.
rollout_plan: 1) Canary in us-west with canary-tenants set and feature flag on (1 day). 2) Expand to regional pair (us-west/eu-central) with low-traffic customers (3 days). 3) Enable for all hosted read-only traffic, monitor 72h. 4) Enable for write-heavy customers and Dedicated after SLA review. 5) Post-rollout: 2-week monitoring watch and emergency rollback runbook.
monitoring_and_alerting:
- Dashboards: lease-acquire-rate, lease-failures-per-region, average-drift (ms), per-tenant shed-rate, total drained-tokens.
- Alerts: lease-acquire-failure > 5% for 5m (P1), per-tenant shed-rate spike > 3x baseline (P0).
- SLO probes: synthetic percentile latency and error-rate for P0 and P1 cohorts.
- Runbook: runbooks/limiter-lease-drain.md (link below) describing emergency disable and manual revoke steps.
retrospective: From the Jan incident we learned: lease TTLs shorter than 1s cause excessive re-election; naive fail-open produced downstream API errors; tenant fairness needs explicit weight derivation. Design updated to use conservative TTL with heartbeat backoff and explicit weights tied to billing/commit tiers. We are adding post-mortem notes to oncall repo.
